all_quotes.quote: We developed a new method using supervised machine learning to estimate BH mass either from position-velocity diagrams or from first-moment maps computed from ALMA CO(3-2) observations.
The core sample is composed of nearby galaxies ($<$28Mpc) and luminous nuclei, $L_{AGN}(14-150\mathrm{keV}) \geq 10^{42}\mathrm{erg/s}$.
We use the high spatial resolution of ALMA to resolve the CO(3-2) emission within $\sim$100 pc around the supermassive black hole (SMBH) of seven GATOS galaxies and try to estimate their BH mass
The present work uses the CO(3-2) data cubes from ALMA observations.
The pixel size in the data cubes was chosen to match that of the observed data (ranging from 4 to 7 pc, depending on the galaxy), with velocity channels of 10 km/s.
All the details of the GATOS core sample and their observations are given in (cite: garcia-burillo_galaxy_2021).

For each observed galaxy, we generated 25,000 simulated data cubes, dividing them into a training set of 16,500 simulations, a validation set of 3,500 simulations, and a test set of 5,000 simulations.
To simulate our data cubes, we used the model described in (cite: melchior2011) and (cite: combes_alma_2019).
The models are fitted with the same methodology as in (cite: combes_alma_2019).

We trained our models during 2000 epochs and took the weights of the epoch with the lowest RMSE on the validation set.
The training was made with a mini-batch size of 128 images.
